notes: A correct solution had to establish what the file's x-axis represents (its 1648-47183 range and ~500-fold variation in sampling density show it is not a plain cm^-1 Raman-shift axis), locate the graphene G and 2D features on that basis, and fit each with a Lorentzian plus offset. At Step 10 the agent instead assigned G and 2D to the two tallest features by absolute height (x~19140 and the ~9% hump at x~33245) on a loose ratio argument, while its own Step 9 binned table showed several far more prominent features (near x~3600-3800, 6200-6400 and 10000-10800) it never examined; under the reciprocal transform 1e7/x implied by the sampling pattern, those ignored features fall at ~2703 and ~1587 (the expected 2D and G positions) whereas the fitted features map to ~522 and ~301, the well-known silicon substrate bands. Every subsequent fit therefore targeted the wrong peaks, and the G fit was finalized at Step 26 with a window-dependent offset the agent itself had called unphysical. The misidentification is material because it determines every value written to /app/results.json.
